deities: Lord Shiva as Saptakoteshwar (faceted Dharalinga; legend says a linga of seven metals)
festivals: Gokul Ashtami (annual festival; devotees bathe in the adjoining river, held to turn into Pancha Ganga that day)

history.dynasty: Kadamba (family deity); restored under Vijayanagara; rebuilt by Marathas
history.period: Kadamba origins (10th-12th c.); present structure 1668; renovated 2023
history.summary: The 'Raj Daivat' (royal deity) of Goa and family god of the Kadamba kings, who stamped 'Saptakotishvaralabdha-Varaprasada' on their coins. The original shrine stood on Divar island (established per the Sahyadri Khanda by the Saptarishi); destroyed under the Bahamanis, restored in 1391 by Madhava Mantri, minister of Vijayanagara, then destroyed by the Portuguese in 1540. The deity was shifted to Narve (Bicholim) by about 1558, and the present temple was built there by Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj in 1668. Renovated by the Goa Archives and Archaeology Department and reopened in February 2023 (Kaavi wall art revived); in September 2025 the state approved a Koti Tirth corridor to rebuild the temple at its original Divar site. The dharalinga is accompanied by shrines to Kalabhairava and the padukas of Dattatreya, plus the Panchaganga Tirtha tank.
